svg.text: COPPER SIDE, mirrored: what you see when you cut the tracks
20 × 18 holes · cut to 50.8 × 45.7 mm · 6 cuts · 10 links · 2 standoff holes (2.5 mm, for M2.5 nylon standoffs)
D2 1N4148 — across the LED, reversed: its band towards the anode
U2 H11L1M — pin 1 at the top left, the LED anode
Connectors (pin 1 is the large filled square)
C2 → Control: Pico 2 WH, JST-XH 3-way (B3B-XH-A): 1 GND · 2 MIDI RX · 3 3V3
C3 → MIDI, JST-XH 2-way (B2B-XH-A): 1 DIN 4 → 220 Ω → the opto’s LED · 2
No ground: opto-isolated: DIN pin 2 stays unconnected, so the
controller’s ground never reaches the pedal.
GND reaches the root through C2 only (Control: Pico 2 WH).
DIN pin 4 feeds the LED through 220 Ω. DIN pin 5 is the LED’s return. DIN
pin 2, the shield, is not connected: the controller’s ground never reaches
The diode is fitted the wrong way for a signal diode, on purpose. It
conducts only if a cable is wired backwards.
Current in the loop pulls VO low, which is a UART zero. An idle loop leaves
it high. The Pico sees it on a UART RX pin.
Ground arrives from the control board on C2 and goes no further.

Red ✕: cut the track at that hole (red bar: cut between two holes). Lines: wire links on the component side (green carries ground). Strips tinted green carry ground, red a supply, amber 3.3 V. White circles: standoff holes; dashed: what the standoff covers.
